title: Operations strategy
overview: Operations strategy turns resources and processes into long-term capability. The current syllabus includes resource constraints, flexibility, process innovation, IT/AI, ERP, lean production and Critical Path Analysis (CPA). This topic is highly integrative because operations choices depend on HR, marketing and finance.
syllabusPoints: Analyse how HR, marketing and finance resources constrain operations decisions.
Analyse IT and AI in operations and process innovation.
Explain flexibility in volume, delivery time and specification.
Explain ERP and its effect on efficiency.
Analyse lean production: Kaizen, quality circles, simultaneous engineering, cell production, JIT and waste management.
Construct/interpret CPA networks, critical paths, minimum duration, total/free float and evaluate CPA.

definitions.definition: Enterprise Resource Planning: an integrated information system linking major business functions through shared data.
An approach that seeks customer value using less waste, delay, inventory and non-value activity.
Just-in-time: materials/components arrive close to when needed, minimising inventory.
The sequence of zero-total-float activities determining minimum project duration.
How long an activity can be delayed without delaying overall project completion.
How long an activity can be delayed without delaying the earliest start of a following activity.

sections.title: Resource constraints and flexibility
content: Operations decisions depend on available finance, skilled labour and expected demand. Flexibility may mean changing volume, delivery time or specification quickly. It can improve customer response but may require spare capacity, multi-skilled employees, adaptable equipment or responsive suppliers—all with costs.

sections.title: IT, AI and process innovation
content: Automation, sensors, predictive maintenance, scheduling systems and AI can improve speed, consistency and information. Risks include capital cost, cybersecurity, skill shortages, inaccurate models and reduced flexibility if technology is too specialised.

sections.title: ERP
content: ERP links purchasing, inventory, sales, finance, HR and production to shared real-time data. It can reduce duplicated entry and improve planning/coordination. Implementation can be expensive and disruptive; poor data, weak training or badly redesigned processes can cause failure.

sections.title: Lean production tools
content: Kaizen = continuous small improvements; quality circles = employee groups solving process/quality issues; simultaneous engineering = functions/stages work in parallel; cell production = teams handle a family of products; JIT reduces inventory; waste management removes non-value activity.

sections.title: Lean trade-offs
content: Low inventory cuts holding cost and exposes problems but increases dependence on reliable suppliers/transport. Employee involvement can improve ideas/motivation but change may create resistance. Lean should reduce waste, not blindly remove every buffer needed for resilience.

sections.title: Critical Path Analysis
content: Create the network, calculate earliest/latest times, identify activities with zero total float and find minimum duration. Float helps managers allocate resources and focus monitoring on activities where delay threatens completion.

examples.label: Worked example
examples.content:
Total float = latest finish - earliest start - duration
Free float = earliest start of next activity - earliest start of current activity - duration

sections.title: CPA evaluation
content: Benefits: shows dependencies, critical tasks, minimum duration and scheduling flexibility. Limitations: activity times are estimates; resource constraints are not automatically solved; complex projects change and require updates; unexpected events can create a new critical path.

analysisChains.title: Just-in-time inventory
steps: Inputs arrive close to when they are needed
Inventory holding and storage costs fall
Disruption risk rises if suppliers are late
analysisChains.evaluation: JIT is more suitable with reliable suppliers, predictable quality and resilient logistics; buffer stock may be rational in volatile conditions.

examTips: CPA marks depend on working: show times/float and clearly state the critical path.
ERP/AI answers need implementation risk, not only efficiency benefits.
JIT evaluation usually hinges on supplier/logistics reliability.
commonMistakes: Calling any zero-free-float activity critical without checking total float/project delay.
Treating CPA duration estimates as certain.
